claims.head: Strength vs. strength
claims.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

notes.text: Noah Hanifin is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Parker Wotherspoon has taken his spot beside Dylan Coghlan. That pair has had 67% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 68:00 together, up from 43% with Hanifin.
Zach Hyman is out (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is expected back after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 52% of the team’s power-play time in 26 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, down from 30% last season.

stakes: The Golden Knights go in second in the Pacific with 33 points, 5 points behind the Oilers, first.

EDM.head: A tough matchup for the Oilers
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage and Vegas will be without Hanifin, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Edmonton will be without Hyman. The Oilers’ best way through is keeping shots to a minimum.

VGK.head: Advantage, the Golden Knights
VGK.body: Even though Edmonton has home-ice advantage and Vegas will be without Hanifin, the Golden Knights have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Edmonton will be without Hyman. The Oilers can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Strength vs. strength
paras: The Oilers are winless in three (0-2-1), while the Golden Knights (14-6-5) beat Winnipeg 5-4 in a shootout on Saturday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Knights second (fifth in the NHL) and the Oilers first (third). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Golden Knights’ record (.660) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.731) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.546), largely thanks to their finishing.
This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 83-72, but only 52-50 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 25-16.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd). They also have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd), and the Oilers’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league (most) and have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd). Edmonton has scored 3.85 goals a game, the third most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Oilers (3rd lowest), so expect a tight one.

Jack Eichel (9 G / 22 A / 31 P in 25 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring. Mark Stone (11 G / 12 A / 23 P in 25 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, with five goals in eight games against Edmonton since 2023-24. Connor McDavid (13 G / 45 A / 58 P in 26 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (23 G / 24 A / 47 P in 26 GP) has a team-high 23 goals, the most in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.
Carter Hart (7-4-2 / .886 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to start for Vegas, and Devon Levi (10-3-0 / .892 SV% in 13 GS) for Edmonton.
